newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN NICKEL PREMIUMS SEEN DOWN AFTER BINDURA DEAL.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN NICKEL PREMIUMS SEEN DOWN AFTER BINDURA DEAL.

text.p: Japanese physical nickel premiums over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices are set to decline in the second half of this year after a cut agreed in key talks with Zimbabwean producer Bindura Nickel Corp Ltd, metal traders said on Friday.
"We've won a cut in key negotiations," said a trader at one of Japan's leading trading houses. "Bindura accepted a two-cent (a lb) cut for the second half."
Traders said premiums for 1997 second-half deliveries of nickel cathode from Bindura under term contracts were eight cents per pound, down from 10 cents during the first half.

Domestic premiums, however, remained well below that level as Japanese stainless steel makers, who account for the bulk of the country's nickel demand, continued to struggle with low stainless prices, they said.
